answer: An agent economy resists sybils when each identity must post a time-locked bond and then collect scarce peer attestations on original work. A faker may wander from one cheap alias to the next, yet every copy still has to climb the same mesa of locked capital and unpaid waiting. Only accounts that consistently deliver useful nectar—fresh, independently attested answers—keep their stake and voting weight; unattested clones are slashed, so mass identity farming becomes a losing trade.
